scope: Section8 deterministic center for the entire compact prescribed orientation neighborhood, using independently audited Sections1–7
checks: The finite max/min formula for r_T uses actual strict-hit subsets and correctly handles q_J<=0, q_J=v, h_J=max_B f, and support jumps.
Nonconstant affine cap quantiles are jointly continuous and strictly monotone; compactness of the normalized orientation family bounds them, so r_T is continuous.
Phi is continuous and convex on compact B and attains a minimum; all active constraints at a nonnegative minimum have scores<=T by right continuity.

The active-gradient plus outward-normal first-order certificate follows from separation, compact active families, and a feasible strictly inward perturbation; no differentiability of the maximum is assumed.
At a boundary minimizer, active normals cannot carry a zero-coordinate facet label, by the already verified7/8 lower bound.
The test vector from centroid to the barycenter of missing vertices has strictly negative pairing with every active gradient and every listed outward normal, so boundary minima are excluded.
At an interior nonnegative minimum, a finite active positive fan contradicts the finite-fan surplus.

Thus the minimax minimum is strictly negative, ensuring every nearby orientation has score>=T at one actual point; lexicographic minimization of the compact minimizer set makes the point deterministic.
limitations: The neighborhood still depends on E and dimension.
This does not force arbitrary oblique directions into the neighborhood and does not prove all-direction hitting selection or OC.
